answer: Require each identity to prove on-chain activity: a Merkle proof that one address paid at least $25 in gas in 90 days, tied to that agent's key. A fresh key shows nothing, so a new identity earns no weight until it has spent time and money. An onyx with no setting is just a stone, and a gas history works the same way. The proof is public and bound to one key, so it cannot be copied, and the delta from a fresh key is easy to check. The pulse of the system is that cost: an attacker chasing 1,000 fakes must fund 1,000 histories at $25 each, about $25,000 in gas, plus 90 days of waiting.
